_what: What this project intends and has not built, for the evidence page. Each item says why it is not built and what it would take. Removed when built, not ticked.

items.why: The house's sensors cannot run a client. Simulated ones would share a cloud host that serves two projects on 2 GB with no swap.
items.takes: a single-board computer and a sensor, about $30

items.what: A mobile unit that takes commands
items.why: A command channel was built and reviewed, then retired: the owner chose to have the house trigger the robot on its own event instead. The lab receives the robot's telemetry and can move nothing. Nothing outside the house can reach it at all, which is the stronger claim.
items.takes: nothing — this is the decision, not a gap

items.what: The dashboard tablet in a role of its own
items.why: It is not a kiosk. The tablet shows the house's dashboard on a wall and is also a personal device that leaves the house, so a machine role would take the second use away with the first: a tagged node stops carrying its owner's identity, and everything the person reaches from it away from home goes with the tag. The residual risk -- an unlocked tablet holds what its owner holds -- is answered by revocation rather than by a tag, and that revocation is measured (D-061).
items.takes: nothing; this is the decision, not a gap

items.what: Lost comms on the household side
items.why: Measured so far only where the lab could break its own link. The hub's link and the control plane are the house's.
items.takes: an agreed window with the household

items.what: A check a visitor can start from the page itself
items.why: A button on the page would need an endpoint holding a credential to start a workflow, and this page holds none on purpose. The same thing is now done without one: a fixed phrase in a labelled issue re-runs the read-only checks and answers in the thread (D-063). What is still missing is only the convenience of not leaving the page.
items.takes: nothing worth its price — the remaining gap is one click, and closing it costs a credential

items.what: Refusals measured in public, not asserted
items.why: A nightly ephemeral node with no grants at all could attempt a fixed list of connections and publish "0 of N reachable" as a machine-produced log. It would turn the deny-by-default claim from something this lab says into something a stranger can read off a run. The cost is the first credential in CI that can create anything — a key that registers a node.
items.takes: an ephemeral pre-authorised key for a tag with no grants, target addresses as secrets, and the disclosure sweep extended over the artifact

items.what: The standby way into the house
items.why: Two personal devices advertise the whole home /24 as a deliberate second way in, approved by nobody. Approval is all-or-nothing per prefix, so switching the standby on would have opened the entire subnet -- and it would not have worked anyway, since the grant names one gateway. The always-on appliance now carries a standby role and will advertise the same two /32s as the primary, giving automatic failover with no widening (D-069).
items.takes: two device-side steps by the owner, then approving exactly those routes; and a drill, because the failover has never been exercised

items.what: Just-in-time access to the action tier
items.why: Standing access to the socket would become a grant that expires.
